title: Does it matter whether difficulty follows level?
html:
Does it matter whether difficulty follows level?

Question: On the default graph, when ideas are not strictly harder the deeper they sit, does the gap between traditional and OSO change?

Answer: Best overall: OSO (α = 0.8, β = 1), follows level 0. Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level and waste. (8 measures; a clear difference is more than 2.7 standard errors.)

  • hardest level: 6.00 against traditional 0.36, clearly better.
  • targets solved: 2.00 against traditional 0.07, clearly better.
  • bounty value: 256 against traditional 8.96, clearly better.
  • ROI: 1.30 against traditional 0.01, clearly better.
  • knowledge found (bits): 77 against traditional 60, clearly better.
  • knowledge per unit of money: 0.27 against traditional 0.05, clearly better.
  • money to the main level: 76 against traditional 964, clearly better.
  • waste: 0.25 against traditional 0.72, clearly better.

Design (fixed before the run): compared α in {1, 0.8, 0.2} × β in {0, 1} × difficulty follows level in {1, 0.8, 0.5, 0} · held the same: a generated idea graph (6 levels × 8 ideas, 2 parents each, sequences of 3 bits growing by 2 per level, composition 0.7), 12 identical agents, equal money each round (f = 0), no flat mint, a knowledge reward of 1 per new bit flowing back with α, no validation (θ = 0), a budget of 1200 · measure: all of hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level, waste · 100 runs per row.

Caveats:

  • A simulation with guessed parameters: it shows how the rules play out, not that they work.
Details

The simple model on a generated idea graph (6 levels × 8 ideas, 2 parents each, sequences of 3 bits growing by 2 per level, composition 0.7); each run draws its own graph. α, β and how strictly difficulty follows level (1 strictly, 0.8 mostly, 0.5 loosely, 0 not at all) vary; the mix of easy and hard ideas is the same at every setting. Held fixed: 12 identical agents, equal money each round (f = 0), no flat mint, a knowledge reward of 1 per new bit flowing back with α, no validation (θ = 0), a budget of 1200.

Values are mean ± standard deviation over runs.
